question.:question/problem:
Find the slope $m'$ of the normal line to the curve

$$
y=(x-2)(x^{2}+x)
$$

at the point $\left(2,0\right)$. Give an exact answer.

$m'=$
{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=(x-2)(x^{2}+x)$. Expand and combine like terms before differentiating.

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)&=x^{3}+x^{2}-2x^{2}-2x\\
&=x^{3}-x^{2}-2x
\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the power rule:

$$
f'(x)=3x^{2}-2x-2
$$

The tangent slope at $\left(2,0\right)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}
m=f'(2)&=3\left(2\right)^{2}-2\left(2\right)-2\\
&=12-4-2\\
&=6
\end{aligned}
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so take the negative reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}
m'&=-\frac{1}{m}\\
&=-\frac{1}{\left(6\right)}\\
&=-\frac{1}{6}
\end{aligned}
$$
